findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define gate_run.status as an explicit enum in the new schema (running|passed|failed|attaching|unknown, per gate_runs.py:320-343), matching how push_status.state is specified.
evidence: Plan enumerates push_status.state as 'state enum ok|pending|unknown required' but for gate_run gives only '`job_id`, `status`' with no status enum.

rebar.llm.gate_run_status returns a finite status vocabulary: gate_runs.py:324 'status is running / passed / failed / attaching / unknown'; gate_runs.py:342-343 emit 'attaching'/'unknown', :346 defaults 'running'.
This is a value vocabulary the MCP wire validator (jsonschema.validate against outputSchema) will enforce on every gate_status result.
findings.finding: The new gate_run schema names a required `status` property but never defines its value vocabulary, unlike the sibling push_status.$def whose enum (ok|pending|unknown) the plan does spell out.
scenarios: An executor authors gate_run.schema.json with `status` as an unconstrained string (contract drift returns), or guesses a narrower enum that omits 'attaching'/'unknown' and the SDK validator rejects a real poll record.
findings.suggested_fix: In the gate_run schema spec, give `status` an enum: ["running","passed","failed","attaching","unknown"], mirroring the library vocabulary in src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:320-346.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify verify_completion_status.verdict as a free-form string (open classifier set) rather than a narrow enum, noting the library emits 'certified' or any compute_validity reason (stale-reopened|stale-material|not-closed|unsigned|… per gate_runs.py:369-383).
evidence: Plan lists 'verdict' with no vocabulary and no enum/string annotation.

rebar.llm.verify_completion_status docstring (gate_runs.py:369-383): verdict is 'certified' only when valid now, 'else the classifier reason (stale-reopened / stale-material / not-closed / unsigned / …)' — an explicitly open-ended '…' set.
The MCP read tool verify_completion_status (_mcp_reads.py:185-197) returns this dict unchanged, so the advertised schema validates it on the wire.
findings.finding: The new verify_completion_status schema names `verdict` but does not state its value vocabulary or whether it is an enum vs. free string, while the library emits an OPEN-ended set (certified plus classifier reasons stale-reopened/stale-material/not-closed/unsigned/…).
scenarios: An executor, seeing the plan's bare 'verdict', authors it as a two-value enum like the tool docstring's lead sentence ('certified or unsigned', _mcp_reads.py:191) and the SDK validator then rejects a real 'stale-material' / 'not-closed' verdict.

The plan acknowledges it (release-notes enumerate every null->absent field) but states no rollback/back-out path or expand-contract sequencing for clients that currently parse the old shape.
scenarios: An existing MCP client reads result.assignee expecting null-key presence or relies on the prior pass-through RootModel schema

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge in the Approach that the ready_tickets anyOf cannot bind row-shape to the full= flag (a deliberate weakening vs the dispatched mirror) and confirm test_ready_tickets_full_and_lean_rows_validate additionally asserts each mode returns ITS expected row shape, not merely that both validate against the union.
evidence: _mcp_reads.py:366-382 returns list[ReadyTicketSummaryOut | TicketStateOut] where model = TicketStateOut if full else ReadyTicketSummaryOut
ready_ticket_summary.schema.json has additionalProperties:false; a static anyOf accepts a full row under full=false (and a lean row under full=true) without rejection
Plan states both modes 'pass the lowlevel validator' but does not note the anyOf cannot bind row-shape to the full flag the way a dispatched pydantic model did
findings.finding: The ready_tickets outputSchema is a static anyOf over the lean (ready_ticket_summary) and full (ticket_state) row shapes, but the actual returned shape is runtime-conditional on the full= flag; the advertised contract therefore no longer asserts shape-matches-flag, a weakening the plan does not acknowledge.
findings.location: Approach — list_of: ready_tickets (ready_ticket_summary, ticket_state): lean rows by default, full rows with full=true
scenarios: A regression that returns lean rows while full=true (or vice versa) still validates against the advertised anyOf and ships silently
A reviewer expects the outputSchema to pin the full-vs-lean contract and finds it only pins membership in a union
